My own independent read wanted 77,190.0, the 1H EMA200 at 77,199.52, which is 210 points lower - but moving an unresolved gate 210 points to suit a fresher opinion is exactly the discipline error this log exists to prevent, and morning's level is better anchored anyway: it is the lower edge of the measured 77,400-to-77,500 liquidation bucket that absorbed 764,091 USD of forced long selling. addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above 78,180.0, inherited unchanged from the morning session. It clears the 78,160.0 bounce high and the 78,047-to-78,133 pocket holding the only meaningful short liquidations of the session. 627.8 points above spot, 1.35 hourly ATRs - a long way, which is the honest measure of the damage the 23:00Z bar did. 78,080.0 has now been lost on six consecutive settled hourly closes and has flipped from support to resistance.

decisionBox.changed: Nothing in the BOX changes from morning - same REDUCE, same two gates, same invalidation, same stop - and that is the finding, not an absence of one. In the two hours between the two reports price moved 156.3 points, from 77,708.5 to 77,552.2, inside a range that never threatened either gate. There is no new information, so there is no new level. What DID change, decisively, was earlier in the day and against midnight: midnight's REDUCE gate at a settled 1H close below 78,080.0 FIRED on the 23:00Z close of 77,677.7 and CONFIRMED with room to spare, the next four bars closing 77,940.5, 77,639.0, 77,473.7 and 77,653.9 without one of them reclaiming the line. Price has lost the 1H EMA20, EMA50 and EMA100, which now stack 78,270.86 / 78,330.18 / 78,332.77 as a 61.9-point resistance shelf, and the 1H MACD has crossed bearish at -163.79 on the histogram. Bias is RANGE with a bearish tilt rather than outright bearish: the daily is undamaged, price still holds all four daily EMAs by thousands of points, and the last six hours are a 620-point box, not a downtrend. I am one notch more bearish than morning on the probabilities and that is as far as two hours of chop justifies.

overnightRisk: The next report is ~02:00 COT, under three hours out, and the risk is concentrated and specific. FIRST, the pool below. The measured liquidation map says the nearest untouched shelf is 77,450.0 (764,091 USD of forced long selling) at 102.2 points below spot, then 77,155.3 (346,610 USD), then the magnet at 77,044.5 which took 1,048,285 USD in a two-second window - 664 points down and the level the market has ALREADY proven it will travel to tonight. Against that, the entire pool above is 145,556 USD across two buckets. Forced long selling outweighed forced short covering 9.35 to one over the measured hour. The asymmetry is not subtle: there is fourteen times more fuel below than above. SECOND, the distances. Hourly ATR is 464.14 after a 96.2 percent expansion from midnight's 236.57. Spot sits 152.2 points above the reduce gate - a third of one hourly bar - and 704.9 above the invalidation, one and a half bars. A single ordinary adverse hour resolves the gate; two reach the invalidation. That is why the resting stop stays flagged recommended at 76,800.0, just under the 76,847.3 Warsh low, where it protects the core without being taken by noise. THIRD, the calendar. It is Sunday night in thin weekend books, with no US ETF flows, no macro prints, and DXY and the 10-year shut until Monday. The Asia open is the first genuine liquidity event and it lands after the midnight session, not before it. The counterweight, stated fairly: open interest has fallen 6.98 percent while price fell 1.24 percent, and the retail long/short account ratio has come down from 1.21 to 1.14. That is deleveraging working through rather than new short pressure building, and a market that has already flushed its longs is a poorer candidate for a second flush than one that has not. The base case is the 620-point box holding into 02:00; the tail that matters is a clean break of 77,400 running straight to 77,044.5.

Three caveats: OKX only, a 63-minute window, and realized fills rather than resting orders.

calibration.rollingRecord: Twenty-one sessions logged. The 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band tally reads four clean confirmations, two whipsaws, one gate that whipsawed then confirmed on the second trigger, and one that triggered twice and was voided both times. New category today: a single report - 30 August midnight - whose ADD and REDUCE gates BOTH fired, in that order, nine hours apart.
calibration.note: GRADED AGAINST MIDNIGHT, because the 21:10 morning session's gates have not resolved: no 1H bar has both opened and settled since it published, so its 77,400.0 reduce and 78,180.0 add are live and untested and this session inherits them unchanged. Midnight's ADD gate at a settled 1H close above 78,830.0 FIRED on the 16:00Z close of 79,346.0, 516.0 points through, and price extended to 79,401.4 on the same bar. Midnight's REDUCE gate at 78,080.0 then FIRED on the 23:00Z close of 77,677.7 and CONFIRMED cleanly - the next four bars closed 77,940.5, 77,639.0, 77,473.7 and 77,653.9, none reclaiming the line, so it holds under the two-bar rule and under the four-bar extension proposed at 27 August midday. acting_helped is FALSE taken whole: buying the add at 79,346.0 would be 1,793.8 points offside now, and midnight's actual 25 USDT spot add at 78,680.7 is 1,128.5 points offside, about 1.43 percent. THE FINDING, and it vindicates a call that looked wrong when it was made. Midnight placed its reduce gate 600.7 points out, 2.54 hourly ATRs, and explicitly justified the unusual width by arguing that a collapsed ATR of 236.57 made the standard 0.4-to-0.6 band too tight to survive noise. That reasoning was CORRECT and it is the only reason today produced a clean signal instead of a whipsaw: a 0.5-ATR gate would have sat near 78,562 and been triggered by the ordinary 20:00Z close of 78,591.4, hours before anything actually broke. THE RULE: when hourly ATR has contracted more than 50 percent from the prior session, abandon the ATR band and place the gate on the structural shelf regardless of how many ATRs out it lands. SECOND FINDING, on the divergence check that has been standing procedure since 27 August endday - it RAN and returned NEGATIVE. The 79,401.4 high carried 1H RSI 76.59 versus 69.49 at the prior 78,852.8 high, so momentum confirmed the high rather than diverging from it. The warning was available, but from a different instrument: 76.59 is above the 75 overbought threshold this desk uses for crypto, it printed on the exact bar that made the high, and the reversal began on the very next bar. Divergence is not the only exhaustion signal and checking for it alone is not sufficient - the overbought flag on the thrust bar belongs in the same routine. THIRD, a housekeeping repair: the 30 August midnight run wrote its report and its wallet snapshot but never merged its manifest pointer or appended its calibration row. Both have been repaired this session.
